text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Personal data use without privacy/legal review","detail":"The proposal mines customer-shared coordinates from support chats and stores them against customer profiles, which is personal (location) data repurposed from its original support context. Only an engineering design review is recorded, with no privacy, legal, or data-protection review.","evidence_quote":"Mine the coordinates customers share in support chats and store them against the customer profile","citations":[],"recommendation":"Complete and record a privacy/data protection review covering consent, purpose limitation, retention, and access controls before proceeding."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No guardrails for delivery-time or entrance accuracy outcomes","detail":"The change alters what entrance guidance drivers see, which can affect delivery efficiency and correctness. The guardrails cover CSAT, contact rate, and promise accuracy but omit driver-side metrics such as time at drop-off or delivery defects/failed deliveries, and any privacy-related guardrail such as complaints.","evidence_quote":"- Delivery CSAT: stop if it falls by more than 0.05.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails like delivery time at drop-off, failed/undeliverable rate, wrong-location delivery rate, and privacy complaints."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Duration under 14 days of full cycle and mismatched with target","detail":"Three weeks is acceptable on length, but geo-level randomization across matched markets typically has few units and low power, and the MDE of 0.5 minutes is not tied to the 1.3 minute target or to variance estimates. The 3-week test also cannot validate an 8-week target, and the learning effect (profiles accumulating entrances) will grow over time, so a short test underestimates it.","evidence_quote":"Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.5 minutes, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Justify the number of geo units and the power calculation, align the test duration with the 8-week target or the profile-coverage ramp, and account for the accumulation of entrance data."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Problem claim lacks quantification and verifiable source","detail":"The problem statement asserts drivers lose time finding entrances and cites a survey, but gives no magnitude, and the baseline of 6.8 minutes has no source.","evidence_quote":"baseline 6.8 minutes","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the data source and date for the 6.8-minute baseline and quantify the time lost to entrance search."}]}
